subject: anaesthesia
title: Intravenous Induction: Thiopentone Barbiturate, Intra-Arterial Injury, and Porphyria

steps.title: Thiopentone Pharmacodynamics
steps.tx: **Thiopentone sodium pharmacodynamics** center on positive allosteric modulation and direct activation of gamma-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptors. Thiopentone prolongs the open duration of neuronal chloride channels, producing hyperpolarization of postsynaptic membranes in the reticular activating system, resulting in rapid loss of consciousness within a single arm-brain circulation time (10 to 15 seconds) following an intravenous dose of 3 to 5 mg/kg.

steps.title: Termination by Redistribution
steps.tx: **Redistribution kinetics of thiopentone** account for rapid awakening within 5 to 10 minutes following a single intravenous bolus, despite a long terminal elimination half-life of 11 to 12 hours. Thiopentone rapidly diffuses from the vessel-rich central group (brain, heart, kidneys) into muscle and cutaneous tissues, dropping central plasma concentrations below the threshold necessary to maintain unconsciousness.

steps.title: Intra-Arterial Thiopentone Injection
steps.tx: **Accidental intra-arterial thiopentone injection** represents a catastrophic limb-threatening surgical emergency. Thiopentone is formulated as an intensely alkaline solution with a pH of 10.5 to prevent precipitation. When injected into an artery, physiological blood pH (7.4) neutralizes the alkali, causing insoluble thiopentone microcrystals to precipitate instantly, occluding distal arterioles and inducing intense vasospasm, endothelial thrombosis, and ischemic tissue necrosis.

left.title: Immediate Pathological Mechanism
points: Alkaline solution (pH 10.5) mixes with acidic arterial blood (pH 7.4)
Immediate precipitation of solid lipophilic barbiturate crystals
Mechanical obstruction of downstream microvascular beds

right.title: Downstream Tissue Consequences
points: Excruciating retrograde burning pain radiating down limb
Severe arterial vasospasm mediated by noradrenaline release
Complete thrombosis, distal cyanosis, and dry gangrene of fingers

steps.tx: These fingers have turned mottled and dusky within minutes of an injection that went into the wrong vessel. Intra arterial **thiopentone** crystallises at blood pH, shredding endothelium and locking distal arterioles in spasm, so the hand blanches then cyanoses downstream. Immediate management stays inside the limb: leave the needle, flush gently, give vasodilators and heparin, and block the sympathetic supply to coax vessels open. Recognising the pattern instantly, severe pain with a blanching hand on injection, is what separates a salvageable limb from an amputation discussion.
steps.say: Mottled cyanosed fingers after intra arterial thiopentone show crystal occlusion and vasospasm threatening the hand.

steps.title: Management of Intra-Arterial Injection
steps.tx: **Emergency management of intra-arterial thiopentone** requires leaving the arterial needle or cannula in place to provide instant direct vascular access. Clinicians must immediately flush the cannula with heparinized saline, inject 5 to 10 milliliters of 1 percent preservative-free lignocaine (to relieve arterial vasospasm and dilute crystals), administer vasodilator papaverine or phentolamine, and perform an emergency stellate ganglion or brachial plexus sympathetic block.

rows: Direct conduit for intra-arterial rescue drugs
Never remove cannula until therapy completes
Relieves arterial vasospasm and eases pain

steps.title: Absolute Contraindication in Porphyria
steps.tx: **Absolute contraindication of barbiturates in porphyria** applies strictly to patients with acute intermittent porphyria (AIP), variegate porphyria, or hereditary coproporphyria. Thiopentone induces hepatic delta-aminolevulinic acid synthase (ALAS-1), the initial rate-limiting enzyme in heme biosynthesis. In patients with partial porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency, this induction triggers massive accumulation of toxic porphyrin precursors, precipitating life-threatening paralytic neurovisceral attacks.

In patients with partial porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency, this induction triggers massive accumulation of toxic porphyrin precursors, precipitating life-threatening paralytic neurovisceral attacks.

left.title: Normal Heme Biosynthesis
points: ALAS-1 produces delta-aminolevulinic acid under negative feedback
Unimpeded enzymatic conversion into mature heme
Intravenous barbiturate safely metabolised without toxicity

right.title: Acute Porphyric Attack Induction
points: Massive uninhibited hepatic ALAS-1 induction by thiopentone
Downstream enzymatic block traps neurotoxic ALA and PBG
Severe abdominal pain, quadriparesis, and respiratory arrest

steps.title: Neurosurgical Profile and Brain Protection
steps.tx: **Cerebral hemodynamic suppression by thiopentone** produces coupled reductions in cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen consumption (CMRO2) and cerebral blood flow (CBF) by up to 50 percent, creating electroencephalographic burst suppression. This makes thiopentone an exceptional neuroprotective agent for refractory intracranial hypertension, status epilepticus, and temporary focal cerebral ischemia during neurovascular clipping.

rows: Protects ischemic brain tissue from hypoxia
Decreases intracranial blood volume and pressure
Decreased cerebral blood volume and edema
First-line medical therapy for refractory intracranial hypertension
Must co-administer vasopressors to preserve MAP

steps.title: Cardiorespiratory Side Effects
steps.tx: **Cardiorespiratory depression of thiopentone** produces a dose-dependent fall in systemic blood pressure resulting from peripheral venodilation (pooling blood in compliant capacitance beds and dropping venous return) and modest direct myocardial depression. Respiratory drive is blunted, causing central apnea, while upper airway protective reflexes remain hyperreactive, meaning direct laryngoscopy under light thiopentone anaesthesia precipitates severe reflex laryngospasm.

left.title: Upper Airway Reflex Hyperreactivity
points: Laryngeal reflexes remain remarkably intact under light barbiturate
Pharyngeal suctioning or intubation triggers severe laryngospasm
Requires deep anaesthesia or muscle relaxation before airway instrumentation

right.title: Cardiovascular Hemodynamics
points: Venodilation drops central venous return and stroke volume
Compensatory baroreceptor reflex tachycardia of 10 to 20 bpm
Severe uncorrected hypotension in hypovolemic shock patients

steps.title: Preparation and Chemical Stability
steps.tx: **Preparation and storage of thiopentone** involves reconstitution of yellow thiopentone sodium powder mixed with 6 percent anhydrous sodium carbonate in sterile water to yield a 2.5 percent solution (25 mg/mL). The added sodium carbonate reacts with carbon dioxide to maintain an alkaline pH of 10.5, preventing precipitation of insoluble thiopentone acid; reconstituted solutions remain chemically stable at 4 degrees Celsius for up to 24 to 48 hours.
